tagline: Attach requirement docs from Google Drive to Jira epics automatically
metaTitle: Jira + Google Drive Integration: Drive Docs on Jira Epics
metaDescription: Attach Drive requirement docs to Jira epics and create epics from new PRDs. GAIA drafts post-mortems from incidents. See the setup steps.
intro:
Every Jira epic has documentation that lives somewhere in Google Drive: the product requirements document, the technical design doc, the stakeholder sign-off email, the post-launch notes. But finding and attaching those documents to the right epic is manual work that often does not happen, leaving engineers to dig through folders each time they need context.

GAIA builds and maintains the link between documents and epics automatically. When a product requirements document is created with a matching name, GAIA attaches it to the corresponding epic. When an incident is resolved in Jira, GAIA creates a post-mortem document in Drive. The documentation system and the issue tracking system stay connected without anyone managing the relationship by hand.

This integration reduces the context-gathering overhead that slows engineers down at the start of each task and ensures that the rationale behind engineering decisions is always accessible from the issue where the work is tracked.

useCases.title: Auto-attach requirement docs to Jira epics
useCases.description: When a new Google Doc is added to the requirements folder with a name matching an epic, GAIA attaches the document link to the epic so engineers immediately have access to the full specification without searching.

useCases.title: Create Jira epics from new Drive PRDs
useCases.description: When a Product Requirements Document is created and marked as Ready for Engineering, GAIA creates an epic with the PRD title, a summary of the requirements, and a link back to the document so engineering can begin planning immediately.

useCases.title: Generate post-mortem documents from resolved incidents
useCases.description: When an incident issue is transitioned to Resolved, GAIA creates a post-mortem document in Drive pre-populated with the incident title, timeline from the issue's comments, and a structured template so the team can complete the analysis without starting from a blank page.

useCases.title: Attach technical design docs to stories
useCases.description: When an engineer creates a technical design document and includes a Jira story key in the document title, GAIA attaches the document to the referenced story so future engineers can find the design rationale in the issue.

useCases.title: Maintain a Drive folder structure mirroring your projects
useCases.description: GAIA creates and maintains a folder structure that mirrors your project hierarchy. When a new project or epic is created, GAIA creates the corresponding folder so document organization stays consistent automatically.

howItWorks.step: Connect Google Drive and Jira to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Google Workspace account and Jira project. Designate the folders GAIA should monitor and map them to projects.

howItWorks.step: Configure naming conventions and trigger rules
howItWorks.description: Define the naming patterns GAIA should use to match documents to epics and stories, which document events should create issues, and which issue events should create documents.

GAIA monitors both sides and maintains links between documents and issues in real time. Engineers click through from the issue to the right document without searching; documents reference their linked issues.

faqs.question: Does GAIA require documents to follow a specific naming format?
faqs.answer: GAIA works best with consistent naming but supports flexible matching patterns including partial name matches and regular expressions. You can also link documents to epics manually and GAIA will maintain those explicit links going forward.

faqs.question: Can GAIA attach files from shared drives, not just personal Drive?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can access any location the authorized Google account has access to, including shared drives and files shared with the domain. It respects existing sharing permissions and does not modify them.

faqs.question: What happens to links in Jira when a document is moved to a different folder?
faqs.answer: Document URLs are stable and do not change when a file is moved between folders. Existing links remain valid after file moves. GAIA does log the move event so you have a record of where the document currently lives.
